sources.name: Ofgem demand connections reform
sources.fact: 2026 reform work addresses a large demand queue, non-viable projects and lack of strategic prioritisation; current thinking is not final policy

sources.name: Ofgem Connect update
sources.fact: 16 June 2026 update keeps Curate/Plan/Connect reform work active; connection delay cannot be treated as site-specific capacity proof

sources.name: Ofgem strategic energy planning 2026
sources.fact: RESP and strategic planning are being developed; final RESP is expected in 2028

sources.name: Ofgem end-to-end connections reform
sources.fact: 2026 implementation work targets connection delays for generation, storage, EV/heating and demand including housing and data centres

sources.name: Ofgem ED3 distribution investment rules
sources.fact: 21 May 2026 rules set how DNO 2028-2033 investment plans will be assessed against growing electricity demand

sources.name: DESNZ strategic demand connections consultation
sources.fact: March 2026 consultation proposes prioritisation tools for strategic demand; consultation proposals are not a parcel connection offer

sources.name: Electricity networks NPS EN-5 2025
sources.fact: EN-5 came into force 6 January 2026 for nationally significant electricity network infrastructure

sources.name: NESO Gate 2 advancement update
sources.fact: May 2026 administrative closure of advancement applications does not alter Gate 2 to Whole Queue outcomes

sources.name: London Infrastructure Framework
sources.fact: March 2026 framework identifies energy grid alongside transport, water, waste and digital networks as critical to London growth

sources.name: London Strategic Infrastructure Requirements
sources.fact: London growth evidence assesses electricity infrastructure planning/funding status and growth-unlocking dependencies

sources.name: LBBD Inclusive Growth infrastructure
sources.fact: LBBD Infrastructure Delivery Plan assesses present and future infrastructure requirements against Local Plan growth

sources.name: LBBD Local Plan 2037
sources.fact: Adopted Local Plan requires infrastructure and facilities to accompany housing and job growth

examples: Demand queue reform is system-level evidence, not proof a parcel has an electricity connection offer
A Gate 2 outcome is project-specific and cannot be inferred from borough or London infrastructure strategy
Future RESP/CSNP planning does not establish today’s available distribution capacity for a parcel
ED3 investment rules describe future network planning, not a guaranteed connection date
Housing growth can increase electricity demand but does not quantify a specific plot load
Strategic demand prioritisation proposals are consultation/policy context until implemented
EN-5 applies to nationally significant network infrastructure and does not itself consent a local development connection
London/LBBD infrastructure strategies identify dependency and need; they do not replace DNO/NESO connection evidence
